name: Quetiapine
route_note: Oral immediate-release tablets in divided doses or extended-release tablets once daily.

discovery.note: Developed in the 1980s as a clozapine-like dibenzothiazepine with low D2 affinity.

tagline: Sedating atypical antipsychotic licensed across schizophrenia, bipolar and depression
summary: Quetiapine is a second-generation antipsychotic with low dopamine D2 affinity and strong antihistamine effects. It is approved for schizophrenia, bipolar mania and bipolar depression and, in extended-release form, as an add-on for major depression. Its low extrapyramidal liability makes it common in Parkinson's-related psychosis.
mechanism: Quetiapine binds D2 receptors with low affinity and dissociates rapidly, producing transient occupancy and very few extrapyramidal effects; it also blocks 5-HT2A receptors.

Its active metabolite norquetiapine inhibits the noradrenaline transporter and is a 5-HT1A partial agonist, which is thought to contribute to antidepressant effects. Strong H1 antagonism makes low doses markedly sedating.
uses: Acute mania and maintenance in bipolar I disorder
Adjunctive treatment of major depressive disorder (XR)

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Seroquel for schizophrenia in September 1997.

history.title: Bipolar mania
history.detail: Quetiapine is approved for acute mania.

history.title: Bipolar depression
history.detail: Quetiapine becomes approved for depressive episodes of bipolar disorder.

history.title: Adjunctive MDD
history.detail: Seroquel XR is approved as add-on treatment for major depression.

history.title: Settlement
history.detail: AstraZeneca pays $520 million to resolve allegations of off-label promotion.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic quetiapine launches in the US.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic CYP3A4 to norquetiapine and others

serious: Cataracts (in animal studies; eye exams advised)
safety.boxed_warning: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis; not approved for this use. Suicidal thoughts and behaviours with antidepressant use in young people (where approved for depression).

facts: Low-dose quetiapine is widely used off-label for insomnia, a practice discouraged by many guidelines.
